_comment: v4.0 declarative problem -- a filled-in starting point. Copy this folder, point the dataFile keys at your CSV names, replace the data. Every _comment* key is ignored by the validator (the schema's root is open), so keep them as reminders or delete them: either way it validates.

metadata.description: Seven days, four employees, two coverage dimensions.

_comment_timeGrid: slotMinutes must divide 1440, and EVERY duration must be a multiple of it -- including each contract's workMinutesPerDay. SISQUAL emits 30; a 432-minute contract does not fit a 30-minute grid, which is what makes Sisqual's Cenario 1 bundle unsolvable.
_comment_temporalScope: Inclusive. schedule_input.csv carries exactly one column per day in this range.
_comment_calendar: A holiday may carry its own demand rows; marking one makes nobody unavailable. hasEve says the PRECEDING day is its eve, so only the holiday's own date is stated.
_comment_contracts: workMinutesPerDay is MINUTES. The matching schedule_input cell is HOURS -- 480 here is 8 there. That mismatch is SISQUAL's; see docs/next_meeting.md item 16.
_comment_employees: LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST. Your most senior person is level 1. Nothing can validate this for you -- author it backwards and every check still passes while the schedule staffs the wrong people. end: null means open-ended.
_comment_demand: dimensions[] is the catalogue of (tableName, tableValue) coordinates -- REQUIRED, because it is the only declaration of which coordinates exist. SISQUAL exports none, so the adapter synthesises it. The three CSVs differ in grain AND unit: days is workload MINUTES, periods and shifts are HEADCOUNT.
_comment_scheduleInput: Every non-numeric cell must be a key here. There are no implicit codes. preferable may be worked at a penalty; unavailable may not -- guessing wrong yields a file that validates and a model that is wrong.

DO.description: Day off - may be swapped, at a penalty

_comment_schedules: The menu a result must pick from. Each code is one shift; a result names codes, not times. Optional -- omit it and a result's ScheduleCodes go unchecked.
_comment_priorityHierarchy: Fill order. Lower rank is filled first, and ordering follows rank, not array position -- so re-sorting this array is always safe. minAbilityLevel is the SMALLER number, because level 1 is the highest.
_comment_constraints: Rules above the contract level -- SISQUAL's labour law. parameters is a deliberately open vendor bag; the validator acts on MaxConsecutiveWorkDays and MaxConsecutiveWorkDaysInWeek and carries the rest.
